_meta.about: Every number the game uses. Code reads values ONLY through Constants.v("ID"). Never type a number from this file into code.

types.Measured value: peer-reviewed measurement (non-NASA), used where NASA has none
types.NOAA value: US government (NOAA), used where NASA has no table
types.Derived: calculated from sourced values; formula in note
types.Game assumption: our estimate where no source exists - must be named in the debrief/sources screen

CARGO_LIMIT_KG.label: Lander cargo limit (packing screen)
CARGO_LIMIT_KG.note: NASA expects HLS cargo landers to land about 12–15 t. Use 12000 for a harder game.
CARGO_LIMIT_KG.source: NASA – Work Underway on Large Cargo Landers for Artemis (19 Apr 2024)

CARGO_LIMIT_MIN_KG.label: Lander cargo – lower end
CARGO_LIMIT_MIN_KG.source: NASA – Work Underway on Large Cargo Landers for Artemis (19 Apr 2024)

LUNAR_DAY_EARTH_DAYS.label: Length of one lunar day (sunrise to sunrise)
LUNAR_DAY_EARTH_DAYS.note: Mean solar day. Local days vary −6 to +7 h.

DAYLIGHT_DAYS.label: Daylight period (equator / mid-latitude)
DAYLIGHT_DAYS.note: Half of the lunar day. Not valid for polar sites.

NIGHT_DAYS.label: Night period (equator / mid-latitude)
NIGHT_DAYS.note: Other half of the lunar day.

SUNSET_DAY.label: Mission day when the Sun sets
SUNSET_DAY.note: Assumes landing at sunrise. Gives Day 15 as in the plan.

TEMP_DAY_K.label: Surface temperature in daytime
TEMP_DAY_K.note: Diviner, equatorial/mid-latitude. Surface, not habitat air.
TEMP_DAY_K.source: NASA NTRS – The Lunar Environment (Diviner data)

TEMP_DAY_C.label: Surface temperature in daytime
TEMP_DAY_C.note: K − 273.15. NASA Moon Facts page says about 127 °C (see Conflicts).
TEMP_DAY_C.source: NASA NTRS – The Lunar Environment (Diviner data)

TEMP_NIGHT_K.label: Surface temperature at night
TEMP_NIGHT_K.source: NASA NTRS – The Lunar Environment (Diviner data)

TEMP_NIGHT_C.label: Surface temperature at night
TEMP_NIGHT_C.note: K − 273.15. NASA Moon Facts page says about −173 °C (see Conflicts).
TEMP_NIGHT_C.source: NASA NTRS – The Lunar Environment (Diviner data)

TEMP_PSR_K.label: Coldest permanently shadowed crater floor
TEMP_PSR_K.note: About −238 °C. Another NASA overview gives ~70 K.
TEMP_PSR_K.source: NASA NTRS – The Lunar Environment (Diviner data)

SOUTH_POLE_SUN_FRACTION.label: Sunlight at best Shackleton rim points
SOUTH_POLE_SUN_FRACTION.note: Source says ">90 %" for selected rim points only.
SOUTH_POLE_SUN_FRACTION.source: NASA Science – Shackleton Crater's Illuminated Rim & Shadowed Interior

SOLAR_W_PER_M2.label: Solar array output per area
SOLAR_W_PER_M2.note: Rigid array, 1 AU, beginning of life. Ignores sun angle and dust.
SOLAR_W_PER_M2.source: NASA/JPL – Solar Power Technologies for Future Planetary Science Missions

SOLAR_W_PER_KG.label: Solar array output per mass
SOLAR_W_PER_KG.source: NASA/JPL – Solar Power Technologies for Future Planetary Science Missions

SOLAR_UNIT_KW.label: Size of one "Solar Panel" item
SOLAR_UNIT_KW.note: Our choice so the numbers are easy to read.

SOLAR_UNIT_AREA_M2.label: Area of one Solar Panel item
SOLAR_UNIT_AREA_M2.source: NASA/JPL – Solar Power Technologies for Future Planetary Science Missions

SOLAR_UNIT_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Solar Panel item
SOLAR_UNIT_MASS_KG.source: NASA/JPL – Solar Power Technologies for Future Planetary Science Missions

SOLAR_UNIT_KWH_PER_DAY.label: Energy from one panel per Earth day (in sunlight)
SOLAR_UNIT_KWH_PER_DAY.note: Peak × 24 h. Real output is lower because of sun angle – game may apply a factor.
SOLAR_UNIT_KWH_PER_DAY.source: NASA/JPL – Solar Power Technologies for Future Planetary Science Missions

DUST_MAX_LOSS.label: Power loss from heavy dust on solar cells
DUST_MAX_LOSS.note: "Almost 40 %" at 2 mg/cm² simulant dust in a lab test. Use as worst case.

BATTERY_WH_PER_KG.label: Battery pack specific energy
BATTERY_WH_PER_KG.note: Lower pack example (ISISPACE). Cell range 150–270 Wh/kg; packs are lower than cells.
BATTERY_WH_PER_KG.source: NASA Small Spacecraft State of the Art – Power Subsystems

BATTERY_UNIT_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Battery item
BATTERY_UNIT_MASS_KG.source: NASA Small Spacecraft State of the Art – Power Subsystems

REACTOR_S_KWE.label: Small reactor output (Kilopower class)
REACTOR_S_KWE.note: Top of Kilopower 1–10 kWe concept range.

REACTOR_S_MASS_KG.label: Small reactor mass
REACTOR_S_MASS_KG.note: 10 kWe Mars Kilopower concept estimate. Not flight hardware.
REACTOR_S_MASS_KG.source: NASA NTRS – Kilopower Development and Higher Power Missions

REACTOR_L_KWE.label: Large reactor output (Fission Surface Power)
REACTOR_L_KWE.note: FSP design class. 10-year life, no maintenance.
REACTOR_L_KWE.source: NASA Fission Surface Power – IAC 2024 manuscript (NTRS 20240011694)

REACTOR_L_MASS_KG.label: Large reactor mass
REACTOR_L_MASS_KG.note: NASA mass GOAL "under 6,000 kg". Team source gives ~10,000 kg concept estimate (see Conflicts).
REACTOR_L_MASS_KG.source: NASA Fission Surface Power – IAC 2024 manuscript (NTRS 20240011694)

LOAD_SCALE.label: Scale factor from NASA 6-person study to our crew
LOAD_SCALE.note: Linear scaling – a game simplification, not a NASA 4-person design.
LOAD_SCALE.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_AIR_KW.label: Power use – Air / CO₂ removal / O₂ system
LOAD_AIR_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_GREENHOUSE_KW.label: Power use – Biomass (greenhouse) system
LOAD_GREENHOUSE_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_FOOD_KW.label: Power use – Food system
LOAD_FOOD_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_THERMAL_KW.label: Power use – Thermal system
LOAD_THERMAL_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_WASTE_KW.label: Power use – Waste processing
LOAD_WASTE_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_WATER_KW.label: Power use – Water processing
LOAD_WATER_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_EVA_KW.label: Power use – EVA support
LOAD_EVA_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_COMMS_KW.label: Power use – Communications
LOAD_COMMS_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_OPS_KW.label: Power use – Operational equipment
LOAD_OPS_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

LOAD_TOTAL_KW.label: Total continuous base power use
LOAD_TOTAL_KW.note: Sum of loads above. For 4 crew = 18.7 kW (NASA 6-person total 28.05 kW).
LOAD_TOTAL_KW.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

NIGHT_ENERGY_KWH.label: Energy needed to survive one lunar night at full load
NIGHT_ENERGY_KWH.source: NASA/CR-2020-220368 – Small Lunar Base Camp Power System

NIGHT_BATTERY_MASS_KG.label: Battery mass for the whole night at full load
NIGHT_BATTERY_MASS_KG.note: Shows why batteries alone cannot carry the night (compare with cargo limit).
NIGHT_BATTERY_MASS_KG.source: NASA Small Spacecraft State of the Art – Power Subsystems

NIGHT_BATTERY_VS_CARGO.label: Night batteries ÷ cargo limit
NIGHT_BATTERY_VS_CARGO.note: More than 1 means impossible with batteries only.
NIGHT_BATTERY_VS_CARGO.source: NASA Small Spacecraft State of the Art – Power Subsystems

REACTORS_S_NEEDED.label: Small reactors needed to carry full load

REACTORS_S_MASS_TOTAL_KG.label: Mass of those reactors
REACTORS_S_MASS_TOTAL_KG.source: NASA NTRS – Kilopower Development and Higher Power Missions

BACKUP_HOURS_RULE.label: Time left on battery
BACKUP_HOURS_RULE.note: Usable battery energy ÷ active load. NASA gives no single "blackout countdown".
BACKUP_HOURS_RULE.source: NASA Ames – Cabin Environment Physics Risk Model

O2_KG_PERSON_DAY.label: Oxygen used per astronaut
O2_KG_PERSON_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

O2_KG_CREW_DAY.label: Oxygen used by whole crew
O2_KG_CREW_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

O2_KG_MISSION.label: Oxygen for the whole mission
O2_KG_MISSION.note: × days. Excludes tank mass, EVA and leaks.
O2_KG_MISSION.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

O2_TANK_RATIO.label: Tank mass per kg of oxygen (high-pressure tank)
O2_TANK_RATIO.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

O2_PACKED_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass to bring all oxygen from Earth (gas + tanks)
O2_PACKED_MASS_KG.note: Oxygen × (1 + tank ratio). Use on packing screen ("bring it").
O2_PACKED_MASS_KG.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

CO2_KG_PERSON_DAY.label: CO₂ breathed out per astronaut
CO2_KG_PERSON_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

CO2_KG_CREW_DAY.label: CO₂ from whole crew
CO2_KG_CREW_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

CO2_LIMIT_MMHG.label: CO₂ limit in the habitat (1-hour average)
CO2_LIMIT_MMHG.note: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 §6.2.1.3 [V2 6004]. ≈0.40 kPa. Game: yellow warning.

CO2_HEADACHE_MMHG.label: CO₂ level where ISS crews reported headaches
CO2_HEADACHE_MMHG.note: "Above 3.0 – 3.4 mm Hg, headaches have been reported." Game: crew health starts to drop.
CO2_HEADACHE_MMHG.source: CO2 on the ISS: An Operations Update – J. Law & D. Alexander (NASA JSC)

CO2_HEALTHY_MAX_MMHG.label: CO₂ level that may keep crew fully healthy
CO2_HEALTHY_MAX_MMHG.note: Evidence suggests 0.5–2.0 mmHg. Game: green zone.
CO2_HEALTHY_MAX_MMHG.source: CO2 on the ISS: An Operations Update – J. Law & D. Alexander (NASA JSC)

FOOD_DRY_KG_PERSON_DAY.label: Food (dry solids) per astronaut
FOOD_DRY_KG_PERSON_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

FOOD_PACKED_KG_PERSON_DAY.label: Packed food per astronaut (ISS planning)
FOOD_PACKED_KG_PERSON_DAY.note: Includes packaging. Use this for cargo mass.
FOOD_PACKED_KG_PERSON_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

FOOD_PACKED_KG_MISSION.label: Packed food for whole mission
FOOD_PACKED_KG_MISSION.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

WATER_KG_PERSON_DAY.label: Drinking/food water per astronaut
WATER_KG_PERSON_DAY.note: Potable water content. Not including hygiene water.
WATER_KG_PERSON_DAY.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

WATER_KG_MISSION.label: Water for whole mission (no recycling)
WATER_KG_MISSION.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD) Rev. 2

WATER_RECOVERY_FULL.label: Water recycler recovery (with brine processor)
WATER_RECOVERY_FULL.source: Status of ISS Water Management and Recovery, ICES-2024-317

WATER_RECOVERY_BASIC.label: Water recycler recovery (basic, no brine processor)
WATER_RECOVERY_BASIC.source: Status of ISS Water Management and Recovery, ICES-2024-317

WATER_KG_MISSION_RECYCLED.label: Water to bring if recycler works (game simplification)
WATER_KG_MISSION_RECYCLED.note: Simplified: assumes all used water goes back into the recycler. Real net need is higher.
WATER_KG_MISSION_RECYCLED.source: Status of ISS Water Management and Recovery, ICES-2024-317

OGA_O2_KG_DAY.label: Oxygen generator output (nominal)
OGA_O2_KG_DAY.note: ISS OGA, range 2.3–9.2 kg/day. Enough for our crew.
OGA_O2_KG_DAY.source: Advancing the Oxygen Generation Assembly Design, ICES-2015-115

OGA_POWER_KW.label: Oxygen generator power (max, running)
OGA_POWER_KW.source: Advancing the Oxygen Generation Assembly Design, ICES-2015-115

OGA_WATER_PER_KG_O2.label: Water split per kg of oxygen made
OGA_WATER_PER_KG_O2.note: Chemistry: H₂O → H₂ + ½O₂ (18 g water gives 16 g O₂). Links oxygen to water.
OGA_WATER_PER_KG_O2.source: Advancing the Oxygen Generation Assembly Design, ICES-2015-115

SAFE_HAVEN_DAYS.label: Emergency safe-haven duration if life support fails
SAFE_HAVEN_DAYS.note: NASA reference habitat assumption, not a universal rule.

SAFE_HAVEN_WATER_KG.label: Emergency water reserve
SAFE_HAVEN_WATER_KG.note: Per person × crew × 7 days, no recycling.

HABITAT_MASS_MARGIN.label: Extra mass margin for habitat design

LETTUCE_GROW_DAYS.label: Lettuce growing time (seed to harvest)
LETTUCE_GROW_DAYS.note: VEG-01 on ISS. Longer than our 30-day mission – planted crops will not be ready unless pre-grown.
LETTUCE_GROW_DAYS.source: Veggie: Space Vegetables for the ISS and Beyond – G. D. Massa (NASA)

VEGGIE_AREA_M2.label: Veggie unit growing area
VEGGIE_AREA_M2.note: Other NASA poster says 0.13 m² (see Conflicts).
VEGGIE_AREA_M2.source: Veggie ISS Validation Test Results and Produce Consumption (NASA)

CROP_M2_PER_PERSON_O2.label: Crop area to make one person's oxygen
CROP_M2_PER_PERSON_O2.source: NASA's Controlled Environment Agriculture Testing for Space Habitats – R. M. Wheeler

CROP_M2_CREW_O2.label: Crop area for whole crew's oxygen
CROP_M2_CREW_O2.note: Per person × crew (NASA range 80–100 m² for 4).
CROP_M2_CREW_O2.source: NASA's Controlled Environment Agriculture Testing for Space Habitats – R. M. Wheeler

CROP_O2_G_M2_DAY.label: Oxygen made per m² of crops
CROP_O2_G_M2_DAY.note: Illustrative: 895 g ÷ m²/person. Not measured crop output.
CROP_O2_G_M2_DAY.source: NASA's Controlled Environment Agriculture Testing for Space Habitats – R. M. Wheeler

LETTUCE_DRY_G_M2_DAY.label: Lettuce dry food productivity
LETTUCE_DRY_G_M2_DAY.source: NASA's Controlled Environment Agriculture Testing for Space Habitats – R. M. Wheeler

GREENHOUSE_WATER_L_M2_DAY.label: Lettuce water use
GREENHOUSE_WATER_L_M2_DAY.note: Ground chamber; most is transpired and can be recovered.
GREENHOUSE_WATER_L_M2_DAY.source: NASA's Controlled Environment Agriculture Testing for Space Habitats – R. M. Wheeler

LETTUCE_FRESH_G_PLANT.label: ISS lettuce fresh mass per plant
LETTUCE_FRESH_G_PLANT.source: Veggie ISS Validation Test Results and Produce Consumption (NASA)

TIME_SLEEP_H.label: Sleep
TIME_SLEEP_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_POSTSLEEP_H.label: Morning routine + breakfast
TIME_POSTSLEEP_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_MIDDAY_MEAL_H.label: Midday meal
TIME_MIDDAY_MEAL_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_PRESLEEP_H.label: Evening routine + dinner
TIME_PRESLEEP_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_OPS_H.label: Work (operations) – tasks the player assigns
TIME_OPS_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_OPS_PREP_H.label: Work preparation and conferences
TIME_OPS_PREP_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_EXERCISE_H.label: Exercise (incl. setup and hygiene)
TIME_EXERCISE_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TIME_TOTAL_H.label: Check: total of the day
TIME_TOTAL_H.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

TASK_SLOTS_PER_PERSON.label: Free work hours per person per day
TASK_SLOTS_PER_PERSON.note: Use for "how many tasks per turn".
TASK_SLOTS_PER_PERSON.source: Early Assessments of Crew Timelines for the Lunar Surface Habitat (NASA)

REPAIR_CREW_H_MISSION.label: Repair time needed per mission (90 % case)
REPAIR_CREW_H_MISSION.note: Modelled for a 28-day lunar mission; 95 %: 64 h, 99 %: 83 h.
REPAIR_CREW_H_MISSION.source: Assessment of Crew Time for Maintenance and Repair Activities for Lunar Surface Missions (NASA)

REPAIR_CREW_H_DAY.label: Average repair time per day
REPAIR_CREW_H_DAY.source: Assessment of Crew Time for Maintenance and Repair Activities for Lunar Surface Missions (NASA)

RAD_SURFACE_MSV_DAY.label: Daily radiation on the open surface
RAD_SURFACE_MSV_DAY.note: Chang'e 4 lander measurement (1369 µSv/day). Peer-reviewed; no NASA surface measurement exists.
RAD_SURFACE_MSV_DAY.source: Zhang et al. 2020, First measurements of the radiation dose on the lunar surface, Science Advances 6, eaaz1334 (peer-reviewed; Chang'e 4)

RAD_HABITAT_MSV_DAY.label: Daily radiation inside the habitat
RAD_HABITAT_MSV_DAY.note: NASA model, crew quarters 0.94–0.95; other rooms 0.82+.
RAD_HABITAT_MSV_DAY.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

RAD_MISSION_SURFACE_MSV.label: Mission dose if always outside
RAD_MISSION_SURFACE_MSV.source: Zhang et al. 2020, First measurements of the radiation dose on the lunar surface, Science Advances 6, eaaz1334 (peer-reviewed; Chang'e 4)

RAD_MISSION_HABITAT_MSV.label: Mission dose if always inside
RAD_MISSION_HABITAT_MSV.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

RAD_SPE_LIMIT_MSV.label: Dose limit for one solar storm (design)
RAD_SPE_LIMIT_MSV.note: Team: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 §4.8.3. NASA lunar study uses 250 mGy-Eq (blood-forming organs). Game: evacuate/shelter trigger.

SPE_DOSE_UNSHIELDED_MAX_MSV.label: Big storm dose in habitat crew quarters – high model
SPE_DOSE_UNSHIELDED_MAX_MSV.note: August 1972 storm, King model, 398–526 mSv. Above the 250 limit → crew must shelter.
SPE_DOSE_UNSHIELDED_MAX_MSV.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SPE_DOSE_UNSHIELDED_MIN_MSV.label: Big storm dose in habitat crew quarters – low model
SPE_DOSE_UNSHIELDED_MIN_MSV.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_5.label: Storm dose with 5 g/cm² extra water shield
SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_5.note: Pressurized rover study, Aug 1972 storm, with curtain.
SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_5.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_10.label: Storm dose with 10 g/cm² extra water shield
SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_10.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_15.label: Storm dose with 15 g/cm² extra water shield
SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_15.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SPE_DURATION.label: How long a big solar storm lasts
SPE_DURATION.source: Radiation Exposure Analyses Supporting SPE Shielding Technologies – Walker, Clowdsley et al. (NASA)

SPE_WARNING_FAST_MIN.label: Warning time – fastest storm
SPE_WARNING_FAST_MIN.note: Jan 2005 event: 20–25 min warning from electron signal.
SPE_WARNING_FAST_MIN.source: REleASE solar proton forecasting – A. Posner (NASA HQ), CCMC Workshop 2010

SPE_WARNING_TYPICAL_MIN.label: Warning time – typical (electrons arrive before protons)
SPE_WARNING_TYPICAL_MIN.note: "about one hour before the solar proton radiation hazard arrives".
SPE_WARNING_TYPICAL_MIN.source: REleASE solar proton forecasting – A. Posner (NASA HQ), CCMC Workshop 2010

SPE_WARNING_FORECAST_MIN.label: Warning time – average forecast lead (archived tests)
SPE_WARNING_FORECAST_MIN.note: 10 of 11 prompt events; 195 min average across 79 % of all events.
SPE_WARNING_FORECAST_MIN.source: REleASE solar proton forecasting – A. Posner (NASA HQ), CCMC Workshop 2010

SPE_PER_CYCLE_S1.label: Minor storms (S1) per 11-year solar cycle
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S1.note: NOAA scale; NASA uses the same scale. No crew effect.
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S1.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_PER_CYCLE_S2.label: Moderate storms (S2) per cycle
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S2.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_PER_CYCLE_S3.label: Strong storms (S3) per cycle
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S3.note: "Radiation hazard avoidance recommended for astronauts on EVA".
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S3.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_PER_CYCLE_S4.label: Severe storms (S4) per cycle
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S4.note: "Unavoidable radiation hazard to astronauts on EVA".
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S4.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_PER_CYCLE_S5.label: Extreme storms (S5) per cycle
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S5.note: Source says "fewer than 1 per cycle" – 1 used as upper value.
SPE_PER_CYCLE_S5.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_CHANCE_ANY_MISSION.label: Chance of at least one S1+ storm during the mission
SPE_CHANCE_ANY_MISSION.note: Poisson, events spread evenly over 11 years. Real storms cluster near solar maximum, so chance is higher then.
SPE_CHANCE_ANY_MISSION.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SPE_CHANCE_STRONG_MISSION.label: Chance of at least one S3+ (dangerous) storm
SPE_CHANCE_STRONG_MISSION.note: Same method. Game may force one storm for drama – say so in debrief.
SPE_CHANCE_STRONG_MISSION.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (S1–S5) – NOAA SWPC (US gov, not NASA)

SHIELD_GOAL_G_CM2.label: Shield thickness NASA aims for (hydrogen-rich material)
SHIELD_GOAL_G_CM2.note: About 20 g/cm²; more helps little unless metres of regolith.
SHIELD_GOAL_G_CM2.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

SHIELD_KG_PER_M2.label: Shield mass per m² of wall at goal thickness
SHIELD_KG_PER_M2.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

WATER_SHIELD_THICK_CM.label: Water wall thickness for goal
WATER_SHIELD_THICK_CM.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

REGOLITH_DENSITY_G_CM3.label: Regolith density (about 1 m deep)
REGOLITH_DENSITY_G_CM3.note: 1.30 at surface, 1.52 at 10 cm, 1.83 at 1 m, ~1.92 deeper.
REGOLITH_DENSITY_G_CM3.source: An Engineering Guide to Lunar Geotechnical Properties – Connolly (NASA JSC) & Carrier

REGOLITH_FULL_M.label: Regolith cover for full protection
REGOLITH_FULL_M.note: NASA concept: ~3 m of regolith protects even during solar flares.
REGOLITH_FULL_M.source: Archway for Radiation and Micrometeorite Occurrence Resistance – NASA Tech Briefs NPO-47686 (2012)

REGOLITH_FULL_KG_M2.label: Mass of 3 m regolith per m² of roof
REGOLITH_FULL_KG_M2.note: m × 100 × g/cm³ = g/cm², × 10 = kg/m². Free (local) but slow to move.
REGOLITH_FULL_KG_M2.source: An Engineering Guide to Lunar Geotechnical Properties – Connolly (NASA JSC) & Carrier

SHELTER_WALL_M2.label: Wall area of a small storm shelter
SHELTER_WALL_M2.note: Our choice (about a 1.4 m cube for 4 people sitting). Change freely.

SHELTER_WATER_MASS_KG.label: Water needed to line the shelter (from Earth)
SHELTER_WATER_MASS_KG.note: Wall area × kg/m². Water can also be drinking reserve.
SHELTER_WATER_MASS_KG.source: Lunar Radiation talk – M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley), NTRS 20210009760

DUST_GRAIN_UM.label: Lunar dust grain size (small grains)
DUST_GRAIN_UM.note: Sharp and angular; clogged mechanisms, overheated radiators, tore spacesuits on Apollo.
DUST_GRAIN_UM.source: NASA – Dust: An Out of This World Problem (2021)

METEOROID_SPEED_KM_S.label: Speed of a real meteoroid hitting the Moon
METEOROID_SPEED_KM_S.note: 17 Mar 2013 impact: 40 kg rock made an 18 m crater.
METEOROID_SPEED_KM_S.source: NASA SVS – March 17, 2013 Lunar Impact Forms a New Crater

METEOROID_MASS_KG.label: Mass of that meteoroid
METEOROID_MASS_KG.source: NASA SVS – March 17, 2013 Lunar Impact Forms a New Crater

METEOROID_CRATER_M.label: Crater it made
METEOROID_CRATER_M.source: NASA SVS – March 17, 2013 Lunar Impact Forms a New Crater

SUN_FACTOR_SUNSET_DAY.label: Solar output on the sunset day
SUN_FACTOR_SUNSET_DAY.note: Half a day of sunlight on SUNSET_DAY. Simplification.

O2_UNIT_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Oxygen tanks item

WATER_UNIT_DRY_KG.label: Empty mass of one water container

WATER_UNIT_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Water container item

FOOD_CRATE_DAYS.label: Days of food in one "Food crate" item
FOOD_CRATE_DAYS.note: One crate feeds the whole crew for 7 days.

FOOD_CRATE_MASS_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Food crate

SHIELD_UNIT_G_CM2.label: Extra shelter shielding from one "Shield water" item
SHIELD_UNIT_G_CM2.note: One item adds 1 g/cm2 over the whole shelter wall.

SHIELD_UNIT_KG.label: Cargo mass of one Shield water item
SHIELD_UNIT_KG.note: SHIELD_UNIT_G_CM2 x 10 kg/m2 x SHELTER_WALL_M2 (12 m2).
SHIELD_UNIT_KG.source: Lunar Radiation talk - M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley)

GREENHOUSE_KG_PER_M2.label: Greenhouse module mass per m2 of growing area
GREENHOUSE_KG_PER_M2.note: No NASA mass for a lunar greenhouse was found. Team choice - say so in the debrief/sources.

GREENHOUSE_SIZE_OPTIONS_M2.label: Greenhouse sizes the player can pick

REGOLITH_G_CM2_PER_JOB.label: Shielding added by one crew member piling regolith for one day
REGOLITH_G_CM2_PER_JOB.note: No NASA rate found. Treats regolith g/cm2 like water g/cm2 - a simplification (regolith has no hydrogen).

SPE_DOSE_HABITAT_NO_EXTRA_MSV.label: Big storm dose in habitat crew quarters with no extra shielding
SPE_DOSE_HABITAT_NO_EXTRA_MSV.note: August 1972 storm, King model, low end of 398-526 mSv.
SPE_DOSE_HABITAT_NO_EXTRA_MSV.source: Lunar Radiation talk - M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley)

CO2_START_MMHG.label: CO2 level at the start
CO2_START_MMHG.note: Inside the 0.5-2.0 mmHg band NASA research links to good crew health.

CO2_RISE_PER_DAY_AIR_OFF.label: CO2 rise for each day the air system is off
CO2_RISE_PER_DAY_AIR_OFF.note: No habitat volume in our data, so the rate is a game choice.

CO2_FALL_PER_DAY_AIR_ON.label: CO2 fall for each day the air system is back on

DUST_PER_OUTSIDE_JOB.label: Solar loss added by each outside job-day

STORM_GUARANTEED.label: Force one strong solar storm in every mission
STORM_GUARANTEED.note: For teaching. Real chance per 30 days is SPE_CHANCE_STRONG_MISSION (about 10 %) - say so in the debrief.

RECYCLER_BREAK_DAY_MIN.label: Earliest water recycler breakdown
RECYCLER_BREAK_DAY_MIN.note: Anchored on the ISS 2024 case: leak after about 13 days.

METEOROID_CHANCE.label: Chance a micrometeoroid breaks one solar panel

SCIENCE_GOAL_POINTS.label: Science points needed for the 3rd star

GREENHOUSE_DAYS_PER_POINT.label: Healthy greenhouse days per science point
GREENHOUSE_DAYS_PER_POINT.note: The ISS Veggie unit is a science experiment, so plant care counts as science.

FARM_EVERY_DAYS.label: Plants wilt if no farm job for this many days

SICK_REST_DAYS.label: Rest days for a sick crew member to recover

SOLAR_MAX_UNITS.label: Most solar panels the pack screen allows

BATTERY_MAX_UNITS.label: Most batteries the pack screen allows

REACTOR_MAX_UNITS.label: Most small reactors the pack screen allows

CO2_EVAC_MMHG.label: CO2 level that forces evacuation
CO2_EVAC_MMHG.note: About twice the NASA 3 mmHg limit. No NASA source for an evacuation level - team choice. The game never shows anyone dying.

FOOD_SPOIL_DAYS_IF_OFF.label: Food lost for each day the food system has no power
FOOD_SPOIL_DAYS_IF_OFF.note: Frozen and stored food spoils without power. Simplification.

SUPPLY_WARNING_DAYS.label: Warn when oxygen, water or food will last fewer than this many days

SUPPLY_MAX_UNITS.label: Most oxygen, water, food or shield items the pack screen allows (each)

SPE_SHIELD_TABLE_G_CM2.label: Shield thickness points for the storm dose table
SPE_SHIELD_TABLE_G_CM2.note: Points of the NASA study table; the dose between points is interpolated (simplification). Doses: SPE_DOSE_HABITAT_NO_EXTRA_MSV, SPE_DOSE_SHIELD_5, _10, _15.
SPE_SHIELD_TABLE_G_CM2.source: Lunar Radiation talk - M. Clowdsley (NASA Langley)

MISSION_1_DAYS.label: Mission 1 length
MISSION_1_DAYS.note: M1 First Landing: 5 days is enough to teach air+water+food packing. Short enough for a 7-year-old first win.

MISSION_2_DAYS.label: Mission 2 length
MISSION_2_DAYS.note: M2 Something Broke: 10 days gives enough time to notice recycler failure on Day 4 and repair.

MISSION_2_RECYCLER_DAY.label: M2 recycler breakdown day
MISSION_2_RECYCLER_DAY.note: Recycler breaks on Day 4 in Mission 2 so the player has 6 days to react.

MISSION_3_DAYS.label: Mission 3 length
MISSION_3_DAYS.note: M3 Solar Storm: 12 days keeps the mission short; storm on Day 8 teaches shielding.

MISSION_3_STORM_DAY.label: M3 solar storm day
MISSION_3_STORM_DAY.note: Storm on Day 8 of Mission 3 gives the player 7 days to build shielding before the storm hits.

CREW_ENERGY_MAX.label: Work days in a row before a rest day is needed
CREW_ENERGY_MAX.note: Work 3 days, then rest 1. The NASA report describes the risk; the numbers are a game choice.
CREW_ENERGY_MAX.source: Game design choice inspired by NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload (NTRS 20160003864)
